periods.summary: Toshiko welcomes Toka, Uta and Kanata back to Wakaba House, but the visitors soon learn she has been quietly enduring neighborhood harassment, rumors and practical obstruction such as a changed trash-lock. She restrains Toka when Toka nearly attacks Mrs. Ito, reminding her that a Blazer must not use violence against ordinary people even when angry. She later adopts Harima's volunteer-work proposal, leading the children in cleanup and community activities. Her patient guidance lets the children choose forgiveness when their bullies confess.

key_events.summary: Guides the orphanage through harassment, volunteer outreach and child reconciliation.

periods.summary: Nishikata directs Wakaba House and is central to Toka's emotional recovery. In the refugee shelter she confronts Mrs. Ito when Ito panics in front of her child, explaining that adults must not collapse shamefully before frightened children. Kanata then asks Nishikata to support Toka. Nishikata recalls meeting Toka as a child, recognizing that Toka had forgotten how to rely on others after losing her parents, and telling her the meaning of the chamomile garden her parents left her. In Toka's hospital room, Nishikata embraces her and says her parents and Wakaba House do not want her to destroy herself trying to be strong. This lets Toka cry, accept help, and later rally everyone rather than chase solitary heroism.

key_events.summary: Calms refugees, then comforts Toka and reframes her parents' chamomile wish as permission to live and smile.
Joins Wakaba House in giving Toka the birthday gift that helps her realize shared strength.
